climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
land: Faces the morning sun. Early light dries the dew, which cuts disease, and the grapes are spared the hottest afternoon sun.

blurb.text: A grand cru vineyard for red wine from Pinot Noir in the Côte de Nuits, Burgundy. Its appellation dates from 1936. It is shared between Chambolle-Musigny, where most of it lies, and Morey-Saint-Denis.
